ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A different epithelial response to reflux

A patient with years of gastroesophageal reflux undergoes endoscopy. Distal esophageal biopsies show intestinal-type columnar epithelium containing goblet cells where stratified squamous epithelium is normally present; there is no invasion. Which adaptive change does this represent?

  1. Hypertrophy
  2. Atrophy
  3. Anaplasia
  4. Liquefactive necrosis
  5. Metaplasia
Answer and explanation

Metaplasia

Replacement of one mature epithelial type by another is metaplasia; in this setting it is Barrett esophagus.

Option explanations

Metaplasia: Replacement of one mature epithelial type by another is metaplasia; in this setting it is Barrett esophagus.

Hypertrophy: Hypertrophy changes size, not cell identity.

Atrophy: Atrophy reduces tissue mass and does not create goblet-cell-containing epithelium.

Anaplasia: Anaplasia denotes loss of differentiation in malignancy.

Liquefactive necrosis: Necrosis causes tissue death rather than a viable epithelial replacement.

Related lecture

Cellular Adaptations (Growth Adaptations): Hypertrophy, Hyperplasia, Atrophy, Metaplasia
